page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz across 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs. The hardware platform utilizes the x86_64 architecture with support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The server includes 32 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU, coupled with a 16 MB L3 cache.

The instance comes equipped with 600 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage and offers 5 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks position the instance within the middle tier for multi-threaded computation, evidenced by multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench compilation metrics. Redis operations and static web delivery also maintain average throughput figures. Conversely, single-core processing scores in stress-ng fall into the lowest decile, and uncached large-block memory read and write speeds exhibit below-average bandwidth compared to peer configurations.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation and integrated NVMe solid-state storage, c5ad.4xlarge delivers a resource footprint tailored for CPU-bound tasks that benefit from rapid local scratch space without incurring external storage latency. The absence of a dedicated GPU and lower single-thread efficiency preclude its use for heavy machine learning acceleration or single-threaded bottlenecks. It is architecturally suited for distributed compilation, video transcoding, CI/CD worker nodes, and batch extract-transform-load jobs that rely on temporary local caching.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.4xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud server powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor running at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 32 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 600 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and baseline networking is rated at 5 Gbps. Benchmarks reflect mid-tier performance across multi-threaded computational workloads, software compilation, and compression, alongside average throughput in static web serving and Redis caching. However, single-core execution and uncached memory bandwidth show weaker relative benchmark results. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external block storage dependencies for scratch files and intermediate processing stages. The c5ad.4xlarge fits multi-threaded computational tasks, distributed build systems, media encoding, and batch data processing pipelines requiring fast local scratch space.
